CRP.notes: No retail dairy cream powder (spray-dried cream) found in Japan. Under the Japanese milk ordinance 'クリームパウダー' is an industrial dairy category (milk fat ≥ 50 %) sold B2B; consumer baking shops list only custard/whipped-topping mixes and non-dairy creaming powders, which the protocol rejects. WebSearch budget of the session was exhausted during this country (200/200 calls shared by parallel agents), so later discovery used retailers' own on-site search only. Re-checked 2026-09-17 under the new owner rule (a real spray-dried dairy cream powder outside 38-48 % fat is a valid B_SAME_TYPE_DIFFERENT_COMPOSITION candidate). Still BRAK: no dairy cream powder of any fat level was found on a page that binds to this market. The only genuine retail dairy cream powder found anywhere in this pass is Hoosier Hill Farm "Heavy Cream Powder" (hoosierhillfarm.com, "made with 100% real sweet cream", "72% butterfat content", 1 lb / 2 lb / 25 lb, US) - it is NOT recorded as a candidate because the seller's shipping policy (hoosierhillfarm.com/policies/shipping-policy) prints no destination countries and no international-delivery statement, so there is no verifiable purchase path into this market. Owner may want to ask them directly. BRAK confirmed a second way 2026-09-17: the two largest Japanese consumer baking suppliers return no dairy cream powder - tomiz.com "クリームパウダー" gives only カスタードパウダー (custard) and cotta.jp only サワークリームパウダー (sour cream); "生クリームパウダー" gives 0 hits on both. This supports the earlier finding that クリームパウダー is an industrial B2B dairy category in Japan. Owner rule 3 (B2B stays B2B): the only genuine dairy cream powder route that exists in this region is industrial - Fonterra/NZMP "Cream Powder 55" (blend of fresh dairy cream and skim milk, spray-dried, 55 % fat, quote verified) and regional B2B dairy traders such as bestdairies.com (Klang, Malaysia) in 25 kg sacks. Tagged B2B, not presented as a retail offer and not recorded as a candidate because no purchase page binds it to this market. Retail shelves in the region carry non-dairy creamers, whole/full-cream milk powders and whipped-topping mixes, which the protocol rejects. 2026-09-17 close-asia round: the search was widened from local shops to the cross-border sellers whose delivery statements do name this market. gourmet-versand.com - the one seller whose shipping-cost country selector names this country - has a category literally called "Cream powder and masses" but it holds only cooking-cream and dessert mixes plus plain milk powders; taste-market.de and pati-versand.de deliver inside Europe only; msk-ingredients.com offers only a bare "worldwide" claim. No dairy cream powder at any fat level could be tied to this market, so CRP stays BRAK.
